message_source_quote: Unlike White-Bear Steering (Raman et al., 2026) which contrasts think vs. don't-think with the *same* concept held fixed, this contrast varies whether a concept is present *at all*.
writeup_source_quote: This differs from White-Bear Steering (Raman et al., 2026), which contrasts two stances — think vs. don't-think — with the same concept held fixed in both conditions.

differences.what: the write-up notes the direction carries a small content component beyond the dominant stance component, which the message omits
differences.message_quote: The direction is mostly stance (cosine 0.90 with WBS-style) but the contrast design is fundamentally different.
differences.writeup_quote: The resulting direction is mostly stance (cosine 0.90 with the think/don't-think direction built from the same concepts) but carries a small content component that averages out over 50 diverse concepts.

rationale: Both documents credit White-Bear Steering (Raman et al., 2026) by name as the prior method the contribution differs from, and both describe the same point of novelty: varying concept presence rather than holding a concept fixed while contrasting think/don't-think stances, with the same 0.90 cosine similarity figure. The message slightly compresses this by dropping the write-up's acknowledgment of a residual 'small content component' in the direction, but otherwise the source treatment and novelty framing are equivalent.
